titel: Why Group Chats Feel So Exhausting (And What To Do About It)

einzeiler: Why group chats drain our mental energy and how to set healthier boundaries.
kurzfassung: Group chats often feel exhausting due to constant notifications, the pressure to instantly reply, and the lack of tone and body language. This constant digital hyper-vigilance creates hidden mental fatigue and social anxiety. Setting clear boundaries and prioritizing offline connection can make digital communication feel less overwhelming.
stichpunkte: Group chats frequently trigger mental fatigue due to endless notifications and the invisible pressure to always stay available.
Many people develop coping mechanisms like ghosting or lurking to manage the overwhelming influx of messages.
Evolutionarily, human brains fear social rejection, making the urge to keep up in group chats feel a matter of survival.
Text-based communication lacks vital non-verbal cues like tone and body language, frequently leading to overthinking and misinterpretation.
Digital hyper-vigilance drains energy that should be reserved for real-life relationships, work, and rest.
Healthy group chats benefit from transparent communication, low-pressure expectations, and deliberate spaces for key updates only.
Balancing online connectivity with offline gatherings helps rebuild genuine intimacy and reduces digital exhaustion.

kapitel.titel: Why Group Chats Feel So Exhausting
Healthy Habits and Returning to Offline Gatherings

clips.text: Managing digital messaging threads feels like handling tedious logistical chores rather than enjoying casual socializing.

clips.hook: Brains were never designed for this
clips.text: Human cognition struggles to process the massive volume of continuous digital communication it now encounters.
Text-based exchanges completely strip away essential physical cues and body language that people rely on.
Current economic strain and exhaustion turn social outings into repetitive status updates instead of creating new shared experiences.

clips.hook: We were never supposed to see this many villagers
clips.text: Evolutionary limits mean human memory cannot handle tracking thousands of acquaintances and digital profiles daily.

beschreibung:
You know that feeling when you open your group chat and there are 287 unread messages... so you immediately close it again?
Whether you're the ghost who never replies, the lurker silently catching up on conversations, or the friend who feels guilty every time they leave someone on read, you're not alone. Group chats were supposed to make us feel more connected, so why do they leave so many of us feeling overwhelmed instead?
In this episode of But Are You Happy?, host Ashani Dante is joined by Milly Rose Bannister, award-winning founder of the youth mental health charity ALLKND, to unpack the hidden psychology behind group chat overwhelm and why staying connected can sometimes feel like another item on your to-do list. Together, they explore why our brains aren't built for constant digital communication, the fear of social rejection that keeps us checking our notifications, and the emotional labour involved in reading tone, self-editing and trying to keep everyone happy.
The conversation also explores why women often carry the invisible mental load of staying socially connected, how digital communication can fuel overthinking and social anxiety, and why conflict is so much harder to navigate over text than it is face-to-face. Millie shares practical strategies for setting healthier boundaries with group chats, communicating your needs without guilt, and creating friendships that prioritise genuine connection over constant availability. Finally, they discuss why the healthiest group chats aren't necessarily the busiest ones—and why making new memories together offline might be the secret to stronger relationships.
